symptom: Global empty budget blocks production while ordinary grants carry no monetary ceiling
direct_cause: Settings maxSpend gates readiness; spendGrant binds only node count
class_root: Paid authorization lacked a shared invariant binding each submitted request to the current user-confirmed quote.
affected_population: Existing nodes and persisted project drafts
internal_only_reason: Internal selection and action boundaries, no external protocol changes.
invariants: Every paid submission consumes a current quote confirmed by the user, not a global budget setting
generality_proof: All paid vendor submissions must consume quote-bound grants; production uses its confirmed quote ledger.

shared_boundaries.responsibility: Every paid submission consumes a current quote confirmed by the user, not a global budget setting

same_class_entry_points.evidence: Paid runtime branches consume spend grant before vendor submit.
Single and batch renderer confirmations use the shared card.

recurrence.reason: Other vendors and persisted projects can reach the same paths.
same_class_scan: rg runTask / assertAndConsumeSpendGrant / mintSpendGrant across electron and src; plan contains paid entry map.

prevention.invariant: Every paid submission consumes a current quote confirmed by the user, not a global budget setting
prevention.strategy: Bind confirmed quote to grant at shared vendor submit boundary.

legacy_paths.rationale: Delete global hard budget setting and readiness requirement; no fallback.

migration: Drop global settings maxSpend during normalization; run-local confirmed quote ceilings remain scoped to their run.
residual_risks: Catalog credits are not fiat. Real APIMart catalog has no pricing, so its card explicitly displays unpriced; official 1K quote is separately recorded.
Account settlement receipt was not available; real generation cost is reported as an official-price estimate.
